name: unit gates — do the named assertions actually protect what they claim?
why: Every gate in this project was meta-tested BY HAND, which /claude-guidance/LESSONS.md §5 calls a tooling gap rather than a discipline one: six steps with no feedback when one is skipped, and the real signal is a break tripping FEWER assertions than expected, not zero. By hand I only ever checked that SOMETHING went red. Each break below names exactly which assertions must fail; a shortfall is the finding.

expect: route auth matrix answers 401 or 403 to every logged-out request except the known-unguarded ones
route auth matrix answers 401 or 403 to every logged-out request except the known-unguarded ones
route auth matrix answers 401 or 403 to every logged-out request except the known-unguarded ones
route auth matrix keeps KNOWN_UNGUARDED honest - every entry names a route that still exists
route auth matrix keeps INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC honest - every entry names a route that still exists
comment bank ownership checks scopes GET /api/categories/ -id to the session user, not the request
comment bank ownership checks scopes PUT /api/categories/ -id to the session user, not the request body
comment bank ownership checks scopes DELETE /api/categories/ -id to the session user
repository hygiene can see the repository at all
repository hygiene recommends no command that silently skips tests
repository hygiene tracks no SQL file containing a Users table dump
repository hygiene tracks no file whose name says it holds a credential
repository hygiene tracks nothing that .gitignore claims to ignore
every feedback target the pages ask for actually exists resolves every literal selector to an id on the same page
every OpenAI request carries store -false and a hashed identifier on both /generate-report calls (relevance filter and report)
every OpenAI request carries store -false and a hashed identifier on all three /api/import-reports calls (relevance, extraction, merge)
the migration glob actually matches the migration files resolves at least one migration
the migration glob actually matches the migration files resolves every file in migrations/, whatever it is named
every model has a table some migration creates creates a table for each defined model
every model has a table some migration creates creates Sessions, which has no model to fall back on
the table count in the restore drill matches the migrations agrees with what a real backup would contain
saving a subject configuration says the prompt WAS saved when only the context write fails

the session secret must not be guessable in production refuses to load with the dev fallback set explicitly
